title: Mathematics on arXiv — 5 November 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: This is an inferred ranking: arXiv supplies no official trending chart, and citation evidence is limited for papers this recent.

sections.title: A Viscous Cascade Construction of Nonunique Leray--Hopf Solutions to the Unforced 3D Navier--Stokes Equations
sections.abstract: The authors construct a continuum of distinct suitable Leray--Hopf solutions to unforced 3D Navier--Stokes from one nonzero finite-energy datum, with strong L2 trace and global and local energy equalities.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim a continuum of pairwise distinct suitable Leray--Hopf solutions for one initial datum, with all stated energy equalities and simultaneous mixed-norm bounds on the strict supercritical side.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Unforced incompressible Navier--Stokes on R^3; the datum is axisymmetric, divergence-free, smooth away from the origin, in L2 and every Lq for 1≤q<3, but not in L3; solutions also lie in L∞_t L^{3,∞}_x.
sections.unique_caveat: The example uses data outside strong L3, so it does not contradict uniqueness results under stronger L3 or Prodi--Serrin hypotheses; the long analytic construction remains a preprint claim requiring expert scrutiny.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract makes a precise, theorem-scale claim of nonuniqueness inside the suitable Leray--Hopf class, including equality in both energy balances; that is a potentially consequential result, but remains an author-claimed preprint result.

sections.title: Off-Diagonal Induced Ramsey Numbers
sections.abstract: For graphs F and H, the authors prove a polynomial upper bound in v(H) for the induced Ramsey number when F is fixed, with an exponent bounded by an absolute constant times v(F)^2.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove r_ind(F,H) ≤ v(H)^{C v(F)^2} for all graphs F,H, for an absolute C, and also give a multicolour extension.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite simple graphs; the main theorem is uniform over F and H, with polynomial dependence on v(H) for each fixed F.
sections.unique_caveat: The exponent’s quadratic dependence on v(F) is not optimized; the authors explicitly ask whether it can be reduced to linear dependence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper claims a proof of the Kohayakawa--Prömel--Rödl conjecture; its introduction reports that a different proof was posted by Zhong, Kashima, and Mao on 21 October 2026, providing an independent-convergence signal.

sections.title: Polylogarithmic bound for the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture
sections.abstract: For every fixed tree T and clique bound k, the authors improve the known subpolynomial chromatic-number estimate for induced-T-free graphs to an explicit polylogarithmic bound.
sections.claimed_result: For every fixed tree T and positive integer k, the authors prove χ(G) ≤ C_{T,k}(log |G|)^{14k} whenever G is induced-T-free and has clique number at most k.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite graphs with |G|≥2; T and the clique-number bound k are fixed, and the constant C_{T,k} depends on both.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a polylogarithmic bound, not the conjectured bound independent of |G|; the authors state that removing the residual polylog factor remains open.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The full paper gives χ(G) ≤ C_{T,k}(log |G|)^{14k}, sharpening a recent |G|^{o(1)} bound while retaining a direct link to the long-standing Gyárfás--Sumner conjecture.
sections.comment: Full text notes no effort to optimize constants

sections.title: Gaussian free field limit for the Airy_β line ensemble
sections.abstract: The centered height function of the Airy_β line ensemble converges, after rescaling space and time, to the Gaussian free field in the half-plane for every β>0.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the rescaled centered height-function limit is the half-plane Gaussian free field, with spatial coordinate x↦√(-x) and β-dependence isolated by a √β field rescaling.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Airy_β line ensemble for β>0; the limit is in the specified half-plane scaling and conformal coordinate.
sections.unique_caveat: The result concerns this ensemble and scaling regime; the proof uses asymptotic expansions for Laplace-transform moments developed in earlier work with Xu.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper bridges a random-matrix line ensemble and a two-dimensional random field, and is cross-listed in probability and mathematical physics; the stated result covers every β>0.

sections.title: Representation embeddings and the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture
sections.abstract: For a representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field, the authors construct an indecomposable module of every infinite cardinal dimension, settling Simson’s third Brauer--Thrall conjecture in that setting.
sections.claimed_result: The author extends a representation embedding so that every infinite cardinal κ occurs as the dimension of an indecomposable module over the given algebra.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A finite-dimensional representation-infinite algebra A over an algebraically closed field k; the conclusion concerns infinite cardinal dimensions of indecomposable A-modules.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is stated over algebraically closed fields and for finite-dimensional representation-infinite algebras; it does not by itself cover other base-field or categorical settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims resolution of a named conjecture and the arXiv comment links a full Lean formalization of the main results; it is cross-listed in representation theory and rings/algebras.
sections.comment: 24 pages; Lean formalization linked in arXiv comment

sections.title: Linear-length cycles in the supercritical percolated hypercube
sections.abstract: For edge-percolation on the d-dimensional hypercube with p=(1+ε)/d and sufficiently small fixed ε>0, the authors prove that the longest cycle has length Θ(ε²2^d) with high probability.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that near the threshold p=(1+ε)/d the longest cycle has length Θ(ε²2^d) with high probability, with the ε-dependence optimal up to constant factors.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Each edge of the binary d-cube is retained independently; ε is a sufficiently small positive constant and the probability statement is asymptotic in d.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is near the critical threshold for sufficiently small fixed ε; it gives order up to constants rather than an exact leading constant or full finite-d distribution.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper confirms a long-standing folklore prediction about cycles appearing with the giant component and identifies the optimal order in ε up to constants; it is cross-listed in combinatorics and probability.

sections.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
sections.abstract: The authors give an algorithm for ordinary K3 surfaces over finite fields, prove that no K3 surface is pointless for prime powers q≥13, and exhibit pointless examples for q≤11.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim nonexistence of K3 surfaces without F_q-rational points for every prime power q≥13 and explicit pointless K3 surfaces for every prime power q≤11.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: K3 surfaces over finite fields F_q; the enumeration algorithm concerns ordinary K3 surfaces, and the abstract highlights a computer-free geometric proof for elliptic K3 surfaces.
sections.unique_caveat: The finite-field and K3 hypotheses are essential; the algorithmic enumeration applies to ordinary surfaces, while the abstract’s nonexistence claim is broader and uses an additional elliptic argument.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper combines an enumerative algorithm with a geometric proof for elliptic K3 surfaces and supplies an explicit threshold/classification statement over finite fields.

sections.title: Floer theory on based loops and fundamental groups of Lagrangians in C^n
sections.abstract: Using Floer theory on the based loop space, the author derives topological constraints on Lagrangians in C^n and rules out embeddings of certain even-dimensional connected sums.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that non-trivial connected sums of closed, spin, aspherical manifolds of even dimensions do not admit Lagrangian embeddings into C^n.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Lagrangian submanifolds of standard symplectic C^n; the excluded manifolds are closed, spin, aspherical, even-dimensional non-trivial connected sums.
sections.unique_caveat: The obstruction applies only to the stated spin, aspherical, even-dimensional connected-sum class; it is not a classification of all Lagrangian embeddings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result generalizes a theorem of Fukaya--Irie and is cross-listed across symplectic, algebraic, and geometric topology; the abstract gives a concrete embedding obstruction.

sections.title: Uniqueness of the hexagonal lattice's universal optimality
sections.abstract: Building on recent universal optimality of the planar hexagonal lattice, the authors prove it is the only periodic configuration with that property, up to Euclidean motion.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim that among periodic point configurations of density one, the hexagonal lattice is, up to Euclidean motion, the unique minimizer for every Gaussian energy, with a corresponding result for completely monotone potentials.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Periodic point configurations in R² of fixed density; energy comparisons concern all Gaussian potentials, with an extension to completely monotone potentials under finite-energy assumptions.
sections.unique_caveat: Uniqueness is restricted to periodic configurations: deleting finitely many points preserves density and Gaussian energy, so uniqueness cannot hold literally among arbitrary point configurations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper strengthens an existing planar optimality theorem to a uniqueness/classification statement; the authors identify the periodic restriction as the meaningful uniqueness class.
